newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Sunday ahead of the Bank of Israel announcement on interest rates on Monday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.93 percent, or 1.92 points, to 208.37 on all-share turnover of 80 million shekels against 92 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue-chip index gained 0.88 percent to 217.18.

"The market looks good and investors expect a moderate rate cut of 0.5 percentage point. Investors all believe that in the long run interest rates will continue to decline," said Ari Eidelheit of Zeller Eblagon Securities.
The Bank of Israel will announce its January monetary programme, including interest rates, on Monday after the close of trading.

"Everything looks good. The Bank of Israel is expected to lower short-term rates, Wall Street is rising and it seems that a deal on Hebron will be reached soon," said Danni Scharia of Capital Securities.

U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross on Sunday met Israeli and Palestinian leaders in a renewed attempt to reach an agreement on the redeployment of Israeli troops from the West Bank town of Hebron.
"Moreover, it seems now that the budget will be approved. I believe that the market will continue to rise until the end of the year," Scharia added.
"Considering the fact that foreign investors were not active because of the Christmas holiday, activity was relatively strong," Eidelheit said.

Bank Leumi, the most active share, rose three percent to 448 on volume of 5.1 million shekels after newspaper reports said Brazilian banker Edmond Safra had asked the Treasury to reopen the tender for the sale of the bank.

Other active shares included Israel Chemicals, which gained one percent to 288 on turnover of 3.2 million shekels, and Koor Industries, which rose 0.75 percent to 28,569 on volume of 3.1 million shekels.
